blocks.raw: # Explore Charts in Reports (Explore Mode)
blocks.text: Explore Charts in Reports (Explore Mode)

blocks.raw: Explore mode lets you focus on a specific chart and analyse the chart data from different perspectives. For example, you can filter down the chart data, split data using dimensions, change visualization, and more. This article covers all the options available in the Chart Explore mode.
blocks.text: Explore mode lets you focus on a specific chart and analyse the chart data from different perspectives. For example, you can filter down the chart data, split data using dimensions, change visualization, and more. This article covers all the options available in the Chart Explore mode.

blocks.raw: To open the chart explorer, navigate to the chart that you wish to explore and click the explore icon.

blocks.raw: # Reordering KPIs and Attributes
blocks.text: Reordering KPIs and Attributes

blocks.raw: You may need to arrange the columns of your report in a specific order for better insight. The columns that have a higher priority must appear first so that readability of the report is enhanced and vital data appears as a heads-up.

blocks.raw: To reorder KPIs or attributes, follow the steps.
blocks.text: To reorder KPIs or attributes, follow the steps.

blocks.raw:
1. Click **Show advanced chart options** and select the required feature (Pivot table or Display % of total or KPI filters or KPI time period).
2. Click and hold the required KPI/attribute chip in the stackable list.
3. Drag the KPI/attribute chip up or down to change the order.

blocks.raw: Note that the chart views are temporary, meaning they are reset when you refresh the page or navigate back to other reports. However, you can still access the details of the chart, and if needed, download the view in Excel format. If you want to permanently include the chart view in a custom report, you will need to open the report, edit it accordingly, and then save the changes.

blocks.raw: # Using Pivot table
blocks.text: Using Pivot table

blocks.raw: This feature lets you visualize the data in a table. A table representation is the default view of a report that helps you to clearly analyse your data. You can also swap between rows and columns in order to draw attention to useful information. Pivot table leads to finding information quickly making it vital to data analysis.
blocks.text: This feature lets you visualize the data in a table. A table representation is the default view of a report that helps you to clearly analyse your data. You can also swap between rows and columns in order to draw attention to useful information. Pivot table leads to finding information quickly making it vital to data analysis.

blocks.raw: For example, if your rows are dates and columns are KPIs, you can swap rows and columns to make rows as KPIs and columns as dates.
blocks.text: For example, if your rows are dates and columns are KPIs, you can swap rows and columns to make rows as KPIs and columns as dates.

blocks.raw: To swap rows and columns in the table, on the Pivot table, drag the chip in row to column or vice-versa, and click **Apply**.

blocks.raw: # Multi-level Sorting (Data Representation)
blocks.text: Multi-level Sorting (Data Representation)

blocks.raw: In Data Representation, you can do a multi-level sorting on the KPI values and attributes in ascending or descending order. When you sort the values of a KPI, you can be aware of the boundary conditions of your data. You can thus view minimum and maximum values, as well as any intermediate values.
blocks.text: In Data Representation, you can do a multi-level sorting on the KPI values and attributes in ascending or descending order. When you sort the values of a KPI, you can be aware of the boundary conditions of your data. You can thus view minimum and maximum values, as well as any intermediate values.

blocks.raw: Multi-level sorting implies that you can apply sorting on multiple attributes and KPIs present in your report. However, the first KPI/attribute added is given the preference. The first KPI/attribute is titled **Sort by** and the subsequent KPIs/attributes are titled **Then by**.
blocks.text: Multi-level sorting implies that you can apply sorting on multiple attributes and KPIs present in your report. However, the first KPI/attribute added is given the preference. The first KPI/attribute is titled Sort by and the subsequent KPIs/attributes are titled Then by.

blocks.raw: To sort chart KPIs/attributes in ascending or descending order, use the following steps.
blocks.text: To sort chart KPIs/attributes in ascending or descending order, use the following steps.

blocks.raw:
1. Navigate to the **Data representation** icon,
2. Change the priorities for multiple KPIs/attributes by dragging the chips up or down.
3. Expand the KPI chip drop-down and choose 0 to 9 to sort the KPI values in the ascending order. Choose 9 to 0 to sort in descending order.
blocks.text: Navigate to the Data representation icon,Change the priorities for multiple KPIs/attributes by dragging the chips up or down.Expand the KPI chip drop-down and choose 0 to 9 to sort the KPI values in the ascending order. Choose 9 to 0 to sort in descending order.

blocks.raw: # Viewing KPI values in percentage (Display % of Total)
blocks.text: Viewing KPI values in percentage (Display % of Total)

blocks.raw: You can view KPI values in percentage to analyse the performance of a KPI and its contribution to the total value. This helps in to decide if any KPI has an overbearing effect on the total value and take measures.
blocks.text: You can view KPI values in percentage to analyse the performance of a KPI and its contribution to the total value. This helps in to decide if any KPI has an overbearing effect on the total value and take measures.

blocks.raw: To view KPI values in percentage of the total, perform the given steps.
blocks.text: To view KPI values in percentage of the total, perform the given steps.

blocks.raw:
1. Click **Display % of total** icon.
2. Drag and drop the Display % of total chip for your preferred KPI. The chart loads and displays the data for display percentage of total feature.
3. To apply a display as percentage of total chip to all KPIs available, enable Display % of total for all KPIs and drag and drop the Display % of total chip on any of the KPI.\
   The chart will reload and show the data of display percentage of the total for all additive KPIs.

blocks.raw: # Applying KPI Filters
blocks.text: Applying KPI Filters

blocks.raw: You can filter chart data KPIs and analyse the results.
blocks.text: You can filter chart data KPIs and analyse the results.

blocks.raw: The KPI filters are helpful when you are dealing with large amounts of data and need to narrow down to very specific data points.
blocks.text: The KPI filters are helpful when you are dealing with large amounts of data and need to narrow down to very specific data points.

blocks.raw: To filter data by KPIs, perform the given steps.
blocks.text: To filter data by KPIs, perform the given steps.

blocks.raw:
1. Click the **KPI filters** icon.
2. Drag and drop your preferred attribute value to the KPI. You can also search for a filter by typing its name in the search box and applying it by drag-drop.
3. To apply a KPI filter to all KPIs available, enable Apply value filters to all KPIs and drag and drop the preferred attribute value on any of the KPI.

You can also search for a filter by typing its name in the search box and applying it by drag-drop.To apply a KPI filter to all KPIs available, enable Apply value filters to all KPIs and drag and drop the preferred attribute value on any of the KPI.

blocks.raw: # Viewing KPI Time Period
blocks.text: Viewing KPI Time Period

blocks.raw: You can use KPI time period to view or analyse KPI values for different time periods.
blocks.text: You can use KPI time period to view or analyse KPI values for different time periods.

blocks.raw: **Report time period (RTP)**: It is the time period that is selected for the report. This is the default date-range applied to the chart. You can click on the calendar icon and modify the RTP. For more details on how to use date filters, click [here](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/date-range-filter-comparison-with-previous-period-1).
